[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Use Case Testing & Error Guessing in Manual Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the realm of software QA, black-box testing techniques form the foundation of robust verification. Among these, Use Case Testing and Error Guessing stand out as powerful methods for uncovering complex functional flaws and edge cases that standard requirements might miss."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Use Case Testing"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use Case Testing is a functional testing technique that helps identify test scenarios based on user interactions with the system. A use case describes the steps between an actor (user or external system) and the software to achieve a specific goal."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Primary Actor: The user or system initiating the interaction."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Preconditions: State of the system before the use case begins."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Main Flow (Happy Path): The default, successful execution path."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Alternative/Exception Flows: Deviations from the main flow due to errors or alternative user choices."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Step-by-Step Implementation of Use Case Testing"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"To execute Use Case Testing effectively, follow this structured approach:"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 1: Review the software requirements and identify all documented use cases."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 2: Map out the actors, triggers, preconditions, and postconditions."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 3: Write test cases for the 'Happy Path' to ensure core functionality works."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 4: Write test cases for all alternative and exception flows (e.g., invalid password, network timeout)."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Example Use Case Scenario: User Login"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"Use Case ID: UC01
Title: User Login Process
Actor: Registered User
Preconditions: User has an active account.
Main Flow:
  1. User navigates to login page.
  2. User enters valid username and password.
  3. User clicks 'Submit'.
  4. System authenticates credentials and redirects to Dashboard.
Alternative Flow (A1 - Invalid Password):
  3a. User enters incorrect password.
  3b. System displays error message: 'Invalid credentials'.
  3c. User allowed to retry up to 3 times."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Understanding Error Guessing"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Error Guessing is an experience-based testing technique where the tester uses their intuition, historical data, and knowledge of common coding pitfalls to anticipate defects. Unlike scripted tests, it relies heavily on the tester's domain expertise and creative thinking."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Common Scenarios Targeted in Error Guessing"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Boundary Value Violations: Entering 0, negative numbers, or extremely large integers where only positive numbers are expected."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Null and Empty Inputs: Submitting forms with blank fields or uninitialized variables."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Special Characters and SQL Injection: Typing symbols like <script>, quotes ('), or semicolons in standard text boxes."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Concurrency Issues: Clicking 'Submit' multiple times rapidly to test for duplicate database entries."},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"6. Best Practices for Combining Both Techniques"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"To maximize test coverage, use Use Case Testing to validate end-to-end business logic, and layer Error Guessing on top of those use cases to target potential system vulnerabilities and edge-case failures."}]
